cues.en: Instructor: If you think that the mathematics underlying the ANOVA test is really hard, really complicated, and you couldn't hope to understand it without having three semesters
cues.zh: 講師：如果你覺得 ANOVA 檢定背後的數學非常難、非常複雜，沒有修過三學期

cues.en: of calculus and advanced probability theory, and high school-level geometry, well, then you are going to be sorely disappointed
cues.zh: 微積分、進階機率論與高中幾何，就不可能理解，那下一支影片會讓你大失所望，

cues.en: in the next video, because you're going to learn that both conceptually and mathematically, ANOVAs are actually pretty easy.
cues.zh: 因為你會發現，無論概念上還是數學上，ANOVA 其實都很簡單。

cues.en: They're pretty straightforward.
cues.zh: 相當直接。

cues.en: In fact, you already know all the math that you need to know in order to compute an ANOVA.
cues.zh: 事實上，計算 ANOVA 所需要的數學，你都已經知道。

cues.en: You've already learned everything already in this course, even though you may not realize it already.
cues.zh: 本課程早就教過了，雖然你可能還沒意識到。

cues.en: Okay, so in this and the next video, I'm going to show you all the math that goes into the ANOVA.
cues.zh: 這支與下一支影片，會展示 ANOVA 使用的全部數學。

cues.en: And first I'm gonna start by describing the hypotheses that ANOVAs are actually testing against.
cues.zh: 首先描述 ANOVA 實際檢驗的假設。

cues.en: So recall from the previous videos that when we think of an ANOVA, we're thinking about a table where we have the different factors that we're manipulating
cues.zh: 回想前幾支影片，想到 ANOVA 時，我們想像一張表格，裡面有不同的操弄因子，

cues.en: and the different levels within each factor.
cues.zh: 以及每個因子內的不同水準。

cues.en: So each one of those cells in the table has a bunch of data points in it.
cues.zh: 表格每個格子都包含一組資料點。

cues.en: And we're gonna call the mean of those data points in one cell, MU.
cues.zh: 我們把單一格子內資料點的平均值稱為 μ。

cues.en: So this is gonna be, MU one is the mean of cell one, MU two is the mean of cell two and so on, and in this case we have K cells, so we have MU K.
cues.zh: μ1 是第一格的平均值，μ2 是第二格的平均值，依此類推；這裡有 K 格，所以有 μK。

cues.en: So the null hypothesis of an ANOVA is that all of the means and all of the cells are equal to each other.
cues.zh: ANOVA 的虛無假設，是所有格子的平均值都彼此相等。

cues.en: That's the null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 這就是虛無假設。

cues.en: And the alternative hypothesis is that at least one mean is different from at least one other mean.
cues.zh: 對立假設則是，至少一個平均值，與至少另一個平均值不同。

cues.en: So it's a very generic alternative hypothesis test.
cues.zh: 所以這是非常概括的對立假設檢定。

cues.en: So when we test directly in an ANOVA, we don't actually immediately get the answer of which means are different from which other means.
cues.zh: 直接進行 ANOVA 檢定，並不會立刻知道哪些平均值與哪些平均值不同。

cues.en: We have to do some further investigation, some postdoc investigation in order to get that information.
cues.zh: 需要進一步研究、進行事後分析，才能取得這個資訊。

cues.en: So what the alternative hypothesis of an ANOVA is testing is that at least one mean is different from at least one other mean.
cues.zh: 因此，ANOVA 的對立假設檢驗的是，至少一個平均值與至少另一個平均值不同。

cues.en: Here I have that written here.
cues.zh: 這裡也寫出來了。

cues.en: So the null hypothesis is that the means of all groups, which are all the cells in the ANOVA table, are statistically indistinguishable.
cues.zh: 虛無假設是，各組，也就是 ANOVA 表中各格的平均值，在統計上無法區分。

cues.en: And the alternative hypothesis is that the mean of at least one group is different from the mean of at least one other group or cell in our experiment design.
cues.zh: 對立假設是，至少一組的平均值，與實驗設計中至少另一組或另一格的平均值不同。

cues.en: Okay, now this slide shows a super-duper complicated formula, I'm just kidding, of course, and this is basically everything,
cues.zh: 這張投影片有個超級複雜的公式，當然是開玩笑；基本上，

cues.en: all the math of the ANOVA is basically just different ways of writing out this equation.
cues.zh: ANOVA 的所有數學，只是這個方程式的不同寫法。

cues.en: This is called the sum of squares.
cues.zh: 這稱為平方和。

cues.en: You can see we're squaring a quantity and then we sum them.
cues.zh: 可以看到，把某個量平方，再把結果加總。

cues.en: So that's why they call it the squares, sum of squares.
cues.zh: 所以稱為平方和。

cues.en: So we're going to discriminate between different kinds of sums of squares.
cues.zh: 我們會區分幾種平方和。

cues.en: There's gonna be the total sum of squares, the between group sum of squares, within group sum of squares.
cues.zh: 包括總平方和、組間平方和，以及組內平方和。

cues.en: But all the different sums of squares are basically just variants of this formula.
cues.zh: 但所有不同平方和，基本上都只是這個公式的變體。

cues.en: Now does this look familiar to you?
cues.zh: 看起來熟悉嗎？

cues.en: Does this, what do you think of, what comes to mind when you look at this equation?
cues.zh: 看這個方程式時，你會想到什麼？

cues.en: Well, I certainly hope that you are thinking of variance because in fact, this is almost exactly the formula for variance.
cues.zh: 希望你想到變異數，因為這其實幾乎就是變異數公式。

cues.en: You can see here I'm reprinting this formula for variance that you learned earlier.
cues.zh: 這裡重新列出先前學過的變異數公式。

cues.en: This would be for the sample variance.
cues.zh: 這是樣本變異數。

cues.en: The only difference between what we're calling here in the context of ANOVA, the sum of squares and what earlier in the course I called the variance, is that there is this factor
cues.zh: ANOVA 脈絡中稱為平方和的量，與課程前面稱為變異數的量，唯一差別，是這裡有一個

cues.en: of one over N minus one here, which you don't see here.
cues.zh: 1 除以 N 減 1 的因子，而這裡沒有。

cues.en: So each individual data point minus the mean, squared and then sum up all of those squared differences from the means, it's literally the variance.
cues.zh: 各資料點減去平均值、平方，再把所有與平均值的平方差加總，就是變異數。

cues.en: Now you might be wondering, why do we not have this one over N minus one factor in the sum of squares?
cues.zh: 你可能想知道，平方和為什麼沒有 1 除以 N 減 1 這個因子？

cues.en: You will see this in more detail in the next lecture, but the short answer is that we're going to be computing ratios.
cues.zh: 下一堂會更詳細說明，簡短答案是，我們要計算比值。

cues.en: We don't actually care about this quantity per se in the ANOVA, we care about ratios of these kinds of quantities.
cues.zh: ANOVA 並不真正關心這個量本身，而是這類量之間的比值。

cues.en: And so when we compute these ratios, we're gonna end up with numerator and denominators and they all contain one over N minus one.
cues.zh: 計算比值時，會有分子與分母，而且全都包含 1 除以 N 減 1。

cues.en: So this term actually just ends up canceling out.
cues.zh: 所以這一項最後會抵消。

cues.en: So we just leave it, we just ignore it for simplicity.
cues.zh: 為了簡單，就把它省略、忽略。

cues.en: But this is the key starting point from the ANOVA, and this is the key realization that everything involving the math of ANOVAs is
cues.zh: 但這是 ANOVA 的關鍵起點，也就是要理解，ANOVA 的全部數學，

cues.en: really just looking at variance, these measures of variance.
cues.zh: 其實都只是檢視變異數、這些變異數指標。

cues.en: Okay, so with that said, the idea of an ANOVA is to partition the total sum of squared errors, which is the total variance in the data.
cues.zh: 因此，ANOVA 的概念是分割總平方誤差，也就是資料的總變異。

cues.en: So we're going to partition the dataset and we're going to think about the total variations of the total variance in the data, as being a combination
cues.zh: 我們分割資料集，把資料的總變化、總變異，看成是以下幾部分的組合：

cues.en: of variation across individuals within each group and variation across the different groups or different levels within each factor.
cues.zh: 各組內個體之間的變異，以及不同群組，或各因子不同水準之間的變異。

cues.en: So it's gonna look something like this in text.
cues.zh: 用文字寫出來，像這樣。

cues.en: So we have the total variance in the signal, is equal to the within group, plus the between group sum of squares.
cues.zh: 訊號的總變異，等於組內平方和加上組間平方和。

cues.en: So within group means the individual variability inside each ANOVA cell, each table, each experimental group.
cues.zh: 組內指的是，每個 ANOVA 格子、每個表格、每個實驗組內的個體變異。

cues.en: And the between group sum of squared errors is basically how much variance there is between all the members of one group and all the members of a different group.
cues.zh: 組間平方誤差，基本上是某一組所有成員，與另一組所有成員之間有多少變異。

cues.en: So within group some squared errors, this is also also sometimes called the error sum of squared.
cues.zh: 組內平方誤差，有時也稱為誤差平方和。

cues.en: So we use some slightly different terminology here.
cues.zh: 這裡會用稍微不同的術語。

cues.en: I actually prefer this terminology because error makes me think that we've done something wrong, but the within group sum of squares isn't really anything wrong.
cues.zh: 我比較喜歡「組內」這個說法，因為「誤差」讓我以為做錯了什麼，但組內平方和並不是什麼錯誤。

cues.en: These are just reflecting if there are people in your groups, if your data come from people, the within group variability just indicates
cues.zh: 如果資料來自人，組內變異只是反映，

cues.en: that different people are are different.
cues.zh: 不同的人彼此不同。

cues.en: There's individual variability.
cues.zh: 有個體變異。

cues.en: But anyway, other people call this the error sum of squares.
cues.zh: 但其他人會把它叫作誤差平方和。

cues.en: Okay, so let me give you a little bit of a look ahead into where we're going with the next video.
cues.zh: 先稍微預告下一支影片的方向。

cues.en: So what we are going to compute is something called an F statistic.
cues.zh: 我們要計算稱為 F 統計量的東西。

cues.en: This is the main statistic that we are interested in with an ANOVA.
cues.zh: 這是 ANOVA 主要關心的統計量。

cues.en: And the F statistic is a ratio, and it's basically a ratio of two parts of variance.
cues.zh: F 統計量是一個比值，基本上是兩部分變異的比值。

cues.en: So there's the explained variance, which in the previous slide I called the between groups variability, or sum of squares, over, divided by, the unexplained variance.
cues.zh: 分子是已解釋的變異，上一張投影片稱為組間變異或組間平方和，再除以未解釋變異。

cues.en: And that's what, in the previous slide, I called the within group sum of squares or the error sum of squares.
cues.zh: 未解釋變異，上一張稱為組內平方和或誤差平方和。

cues.en: So different terms.
cues.zh: 只是術語不同。

cues.en: And now to make things even more confusing, I'm gonna throw up some other terms here.
cues.zh: 為了讓事情更混亂，再加上一些其他術語。

cues.en: So we're gonna say that the F statistic in the ANOVA, is all of the variance, all of the variation in the data
cues.zh: 我們可以說，ANOVA 的 F 統計量，是資料中所有能夠

cues.en: that we can attribute to the factors in our ANOVA or if this is a one-factor ANOVA, if it's a one way ANOVA, then this would be due to the levels within each factor,
cues.zh: 歸因於 ANOVA 因子的變異；如果是單因子 ANOVA，就歸因於該因子內的水準，

cues.en: divided by the natural variation.
cues.zh: 再除以自然變異。

cues.en: So that's just how much natural variability there is in the data, which is not attributable to the experimental factors.
cues.zh: 也就是資料中不能歸因於實驗因子的自然變異程度。

cues.en: Okay, now to make this even more clear, I'm gonna show you some pictures.
cues.zh: 為了更清楚，畫幾張圖。

cues.en: So imagine this circle here corresponds to all of the variance in the dataset, all of the variance, the entire variability, the sum of,
cues.zh: 假設這個圓表示資料集中所有變異、全部變動，也就是

cues.en: the total sum of squares, all the variants.
cues.zh: 總平方和、所有變異。

cues.en: And what we want to do with an ANOVA, is parcellate the error variance, or all of the variance, into two pieces.
cues.zh: ANOVA 要把誤差變異，或者說全部變異，分成兩部分。

cues.en: We have the piece that is explained due to the factors or the levels within each factor, that is the between groups variation,
cues.zh: 一部分可以由因子或因子內的水準解釋，也就是組間變異，

cues.en: and then we have the rest of the variance, which is unexplained.
cues.zh: 其餘部分則無法解釋。

cues.en: It's due to natural variation, it's within group variance or error sum of squared.
cues.zh: 它來自自然變異，是組內變異，或誤差平方和。

cues.en: Okay, and then when the explained variance is much higher than the unexplained variance, then we would say that the ANOVA is statistically significant.
cues.zh: 當已解釋變異遠高於未解釋變異，就說 ANOVA 達到統計顯著。

cues.en: Now of course, how much, exactly what this ratio needs to be, depends on a variety of factors, like degrees of freedom and so on.
cues.zh: 當然，這個比值確切需要多大，取決於各種因素，例如自由度等等。

cues.en: We'll get to that in a moment.
cues.zh: 稍後會談到。

cues.en: But this is a concept.
cues.zh: 這裡先說概念。

cues.en: And then you can imagine this complementary situation where the variation in the data that's due to individual variability, measurement, noise
cues.zh: 也可以想像相反的情況，資料中的變異來自個體差異、量測、雜訊，

cues.en: sampling variability, other sources of variance that are not due to the factors that we are looking at in our ANOVA.
cues.zh: 抽樣變異，以及其他並非 ANOVA 所研究因子的變異來源。

cues.en: So when that variance is a lot larger than the variance that we are introducing through our experiment, then we would say that the ANOVA is not
cues.zh: 當這種變異，遠大於實驗所引入的變異時，就說 ANOVA 未達

cues.en: statistically significant.
cues.zh: 統計顯著。

cues.en: So this is the concept.
cues.zh: 概念就是這樣。

cues.en: It's also interesting to note before even talking about this F statistic, I'll talk about this more in the next video, but you can also see that this must be a positive quantity.
cues.zh: 甚至還沒談 F 統計量之前，就能注意到它必定是正的，下一支影片會再說明。

cues.en: It's never going to be negative.
cues.zh: 它絕不會是負的。

cues.en: And that's because what we are looking at with ANOVA is variances and ratios of variances.
cues.zh: 因為 ANOVA 看的是變異數，以及變異數的比值。

cues.en: So variances are strictly non-negative quantities.
cues.zh: 變異數嚴格來說是非負數。

cues.en: You can see that when looking at these equations here, essentially, we are squaring terms and then summing them together.
cues.zh: 看這些方程式就知道，基本上先把各項平方，再加總。

cues.en: Now, you can never square a term and get a negative number, except for complex numbers of course, but we're not worried about that.
cues.zh: 一個項平方後不可能得到負數，當然複數例外，但這裡不考慮。

cues.en: We're just working with real numbers here.
cues.zh: 我們只處理實數。

cues.en: So you can never square a number and get a negative number.
cues.zh: 所以數字平方，不可能得到負數。

cues.en: So everything in the ANOVA results is going to be dealing with positive numbers and ratios of positive numbers.
cues.zh: ANOVA 結果都會處理正數，以及正數之間的比值。

cues.en: So the F statistic is going to be a positive number, and we want this to be large.
cues.zh: 因此 F 統計量會是正數，而且我們希望它很大。

cues.en: When it's large, it means that there's a lot of variability related to our experimental manipulations.
cues.zh: 很大表示，有很多變異與實驗操弄有關。

cues.en: And when it's small, it means that small indicating, closer to zero, then that indicates that there's more variability just because of natural individual variations,
cues.zh: 很小，也就是接近 0，表示自然的個體變異，

cues.en: sampling variability, noise, and so on, than what we can account for with the the independent variables.
cues.zh: 抽樣變異、雜訊等等，比自變數能解釋的變異更多。

cues.en: All right, so I hope this makes sense.
cues.zh: 希望這樣合理。

cues.en: I hope this is conceptually meaningful and clear.
cues.zh: 希望概念清楚、有意義。

cues.en: What I wanna do now is start getting a little bit more into the math, and that's basically by, I'm showing you the different ways that we modify that fundamental sum of squared formula
cues.zh: 接著更深入一點數學，基本上就是展示，如何修改幾張投影片之前介紹的

cues.en: that I showed a few slides ago.
cues.zh: 基本平方和公式。

cues.en: Okay, so we have the sum of squares total, the sum of squares between, this is between the groups or between the levels, or between the factors.
cues.zh: 有總平方和、組間平方和，也就是群組之間、水準之間，或因子之間，

cues.en: And we have the sum of squares within.
cues.zh: 以及組內平方和。

cues.en: And so this would be within, the individuals within each level.
cues.zh: 也就是每個水準內，個體之間的變異。

cues.en: Okay, so what you first notice, just by glancing at these equations really, really quickly, you notice that they all look kind of like the same variance thing.
cues.zh: 快速看這些方程式，首先會注意到，它們看起來都是類似的變異數形式。

cues.en: So we're always taking the data minus the mean, squaring it and summing it.
cues.zh: 總是取資料減去平均值、平方，再加總。

cues.en: So that is consistent across here.
cues.zh: 這點始終一致。

cues.en: What differs is where the data points come from and what exactly we're taking the average over.
cues.zh: 差別在於資料點來自哪裡，以及究竟對哪些資料求平均。

cues.en: So let's start with our sum of squares total.
cues.zh: 先看總平方和。

cues.en: So we are working here with a one-way ANOVA.
cues.zh: 這裡研究單因子 ANOVA。

cues.en: So let's imagine we have one factor and multiple levels.
cues.zh: 假設有一個因子、多個水準。

cues.en: So the sum of square's total, this is the total variance in the entire dataset.
cues.zh: 總平方和，是整個資料集中的總變異。

cues.en: We are taking the global mean of all the data, and then we are looking at every single individual within every single group and or every single level,
cues.zh: 取所有資料的整體平均值，再檢視每個群組或每個水準中的每一位個體，

cues.en: and computing the variants across those.
cues.zh: 計算它們的變異。

cues.en: So the sum of squares total is basically like, the entire variability that's present in the dataset, ignoring all of the levels.
cues.zh: 所以，總平方和基本上就是忽略所有水準後，資料集中存在的全部變異。

cues.en: Okay, and then we have the sum of squares between, and remember this is between the different levels.
cues.zh: 接著是組間平方和，記得，指不同水準之間。

cues.en: So this is the variability that we can attribute to the different levels of our factor.
cues.zh: 這是可以歸因於因子不同水準的變異。

cues.en: This is the thing that we are manipulating in our experiment or the, the different groups that we've organized based on some characteristic.
cues.zh: 也就是實驗中操弄的項目，或根據某些特徵組織成的不同群組。

cues.en: So the mean here is still the global mean, it's still the mean of the entire dataset, but we're actually ignoring all of the individuals here.
cues.zh: 這裡仍使用整體平均值，也就是整個資料集的平均值，但實際上忽略所有個體。

cues.en: And now what we're looking at is the mean within each group, or the mean within each level, minus the global mean.
cues.zh: 現在看的是各組或各水準內的平均值，減去整體平均值。

cues.en: So notice that in this between group sum of squared term, we're averaging over all the individuals.
cues.zh: 注意，組間平方和這一項，是先對所有個體平均。

cues.en: We no longer have individuals within a group.
cues.zh: 不再保有群組內的個體。

cues.en: We only have the groups.
cues.zh: 只留下群組。

cues.en: So we ignore all of the individual variability in this SS between term.
cues.zh: 因此，組間 SS 這一項，忽略了所有個體變異。

cues.en: Okay, and then finally we have the SS within.
cues.zh: 最後是組內 SS。

cues.en: And as I mentioned a few moments ago, sometimes people call this the sum of squared errors, but other people call it within,
cues.zh: 如剛才提到，有些人稱它為誤差平方和，另一些人則稱為組內平方和。

cues.en: I prefer the term within because yeah, I think it's a little weird to call the differences between different people errors, like, that's a mistake.
cues.zh: 我比較喜歡「組內」，因為把不同人的差異叫作誤差，好像說那是個錯誤，有點奇怪。

cues.en: Anyway, okay, again, we have a similar looking variance here, okay, here is the key difference.
cues.zh: 同樣，這裡有類似的變異數形式，關鍵差異在這裡。

cues.en: Now we are no longer computing the distance to the global mean, but only the distance to the mean within each specific group.
cues.zh: 現在計算的不再是與整體平均值的距離，而只是與各自群組內平均值的距離。

cues.en: So within each specific level.
cues.zh: 也就是各個水準內。

cues.en: So that means that each or different individuals are going to be subtracting from a different mean.
cues.zh: 因此，不同個體所減去的平均值會不同。

cues.en: So this is the mean within the group.
cues.zh: 這是群組內的平均值。

cues.en: And then we have the individuals within each group, and then we have all of the different groups or the different levels within our factor.
cues.zh: 這裡有各組內的個體，再加上因子內所有不同群組、不同水準。

cues.en: So that is how we break up the sum of squared errors, the total sum of squared, the sum of squared between and the sum of squared within.
cues.zh: 這就是如何拆分總平方和、組間平方和，以及組內平方和。

cues.en: Now each one of these quantities has a degree of freedom or degrees of freedom term associated with it.
cues.zh: 每個量都有對應的自由度項。

cues.en: I would like you to pause the video and think about what are the three degrees of freedom going to be for these three different quantities.
cues.zh: 希望你暫停影片，想想這三種不同的量，各自的自由度是多少。

cues.en: They each get their own degrees of freedom.
cues.zh: 它們各有自己的自由度。

cues.en: Now, I would like you to think back, and remember the video where I first introduced the concept of degrees of freedom.
cues.zh: 回想最初介紹自由度概念的影片。

cues.en: And I said that in general, the computation for degrees of freedom is the number of individuals, minus the number of parameters.
cues.zh: 當時說，一般而言，自由度的計算是個體數減去參數數量。

cues.en: So that's like a general formula, and I would like you to keep that in mind when thinking about how many degrees of freedom are here, how many degrees of freedom are here, and how many degrees of freedom are here.
cues.zh: 這是一個一般公式，希望你記著它，思考這裡、這裡，以及這裡分別有多少自由度。

cues.en: All right, pause the video.
cues.zh: 好，暫停影片。

cues.en: Okay, how did you do?
cues.zh: 想得如何？

cues.en: Did you figure it out?
cues.zh: 你算出來了嗎？

cues.en: Let's see, I certainly hope you at least gave it a good guess and a critical thought.
cues.zh: 希望你至少認真猜過，批判性地思考過。

cues.en: Even if you got it wrong, the important part is that you are thinking about it.
cues.zh: 即使答錯，重要的是有思考。

cues.en: So here's the answer, the degrees of freedom total, is N minus one, where N is the total number of subjects.
cues.zh: 答案是，總自由度是 N 減 1，N 是受試者總數。

cues.en: And this one should be fairly straightforward because this is like computing the variance.
cues.zh: 這個應該相當直接，因為類似計算變異數。

cues.en: So you know, the variance term has one over N minus one.
cues.zh: 你知道變異數有 1 除以 N 減 1 這一項。

cues.en: So N minus one degrees of freedom for the sum of squares total.
cues.zh: 所以，總平方和的自由度是 N 減 1。

cues.en: Then we get to the sum squares between, and this is kind of the weird one.
cues.zh: 接著是組間平方和，這一個比較奇怪。

cues.en: It actually turns out to be K minus one, where K is the number of levels.
cues.zh: 它其實是 K 減 1，K 是水準數。

cues.en: Now maybe you call this a different parameter but it doesn't matter what you labeled this as.
cues.zh: 你也許用別的參數名稱，但標成什麼並不重要。

cues.en: But it's the number of levels that we are that we have in our factor, minus one.
cues.zh: 就是因子中的水準數減 1。

cues.en: Now the reason why is that we are averaging over all the individuals.
cues.zh: 原因是，我們對所有個體平均。

cues.en: We no longer have any individual data points here.
cues.zh: 這裡不再有個別資料點。

cues.en: We only have the average of each of the levels here.
cues.zh: 只剩各水準的平均值。

cues.en: So we still have N minus one, but now N turns out to be K.
cues.zh: 所以仍是 N 減 1，只是現在 N 其實變成 K。

cues.en: Okay, and then the tricky one, which is probably the hardest to to figure out for the degrees of freedom, is the SS within the sum of squared within.
cues.zh: 比較棘手、自由度可能最難想出來的，是組內 SS，也就是組內平方和。

cues.en: So that turns out to be N minus K.
cues.zh: 結果是 N 減 K。

cues.en: And the reason why it's N minus K is that, well, the N comes from the fact that we are pooling together all of the, or considering all of the individuals in our data.
cues.zh: N 減 K 的原因是，N 來自我們把資料中的所有個體合在一起考慮。

cues.en: So all the individuals within each level and then all the levels.
cues.zh: 也就是各水準內的所有個體，再涵蓋全部水準。

cues.en: So that's still all of the people that we've measured in our data set.
cues.zh: 因此仍是資料集中量測的所有人。

cues.en: So that would be N.
cues.zh: 那就是 N。

cues.en: And then the K instead of one actually comes because we have K different means here.
cues.zh: 而減去 K，不是 1，是因為這裡有 K 個不同平均值。

cues.en: Here we had one mean.
cues.zh: 這裡只有一個平均值。

cues.en: So there we have one parameter.
cues.zh: 所以只有一個參數。

cues.en: Here we have K distinct means, again, where K refers to the number of levels.
cues.zh: 這裡有 K 個不同平均值，K 同樣指水準數。

cues.en: So there's K different means, there's K parameters.
cues.zh: 有 K 個平均值，也就有 K 個參數。

cues.en: So in all these cases we still have the number of individuals minus the number of parameters.
cues.zh: 所以所有情況都是個體數減去參數數量。

cues.en: And that is what defines the degrees of freedom for each of these variance quantities.
cues.zh: 這定義了各個變異量的自由度。

cues.en: Last thing I wanna mention here is that everything that I'm talking about in this video is just for a one-way ANOVA, a one-factor ANOVA with multiple levels within that factor.
cues.zh: 最後提醒，這支影片全部只針對單因子 ANOVA，也就是一個因子內有多個水準。

cues.en: That's really just done for simplicity here, to introduce the math of the ANOVA in a simple way.
cues.zh: 只是為了簡單，以容易的方式介紹 ANOVA 數學。

cues.en: In later videos, I'm gonna talk about how to adapt this stuff to multi-way ANOVAs, but it's this, exactly the same concept.
cues.zh: 之後會談如何調整成多因子 ANOVA，但概念完全相同。

cues.en: We just have to introduce a couple of other terms.
cues.zh: 只需要多引入幾個項。

cues.en: So I hope you enjoyed this video.
cues.zh: 希望你喜歡這支影片。

cues.en: You saw that the ANOVA, the math underlying the ANOVA, is pretty straightforward.
cues.zh: 你看到 ANOVA 背後的數學相當直接。

cues.en: It's really just the variance and computing variance in different ways.
cues.zh: 其實只是變異數，以及用不同方式計算變異數。
